feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader with clear public-sector specialization and solid evidence of progression and scope. It reads polished and substantive, but it is slightly dense and somewhat repetitive across skills sections, which reduces scanability and impact.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong career progression at NACo culminating in director-level ownership of web, analytics, governance, video, and budget.  
- Good use of scale and credibility markers: “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” “50+ internal publishers,” and named tools/platforms strengthen impact.  
- Writing is generally polished, professional, and consistent in tone, with no obvious misspellings or major grammar errors.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would tighten structure and make key differentiators stand out faster.  
- Add more outcome-focused results beyond scope/build activity, especially for freelance and earlier roles: quantify improvements in engagement, efficiency, adoption, cost savings, or campaign performance.  
- Fix minor style inconsistencies: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; punctuation/bullet formatting in work entries is uneven; “Coleman DAVIS” in all caps feels stylistically inconsistent with the rest of the CV.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible positioning with clear seniority and public-sector focus. However, it overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience, and could be sharper by foregrounding scale and outcomes.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten to one concise value statement plus one scope statement; reduce list-like phrasing.
- Add scale or context from recent roles, e.g. “10,000+ page platforms,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ publishers.”
- Replace “Leads” with first-person implied summary language for consistency: “Specializes in” or “Experienced in.”
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing large public-sector web platforms and communications operations. Specializes in digital governance, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production, and AI-enabled search and content experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with core competencies and recent projects; “AI-enabled search and content experiences” is more specific.
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” repeats themes already covered in the subtitle and skills sections.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block largely repeats the header and Topline Skills. It would be sharper if grouped around distinctive leadership strengths and phrased more consistently.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and standardize phrasing; use parallel noun forms and avoid mixing systems, operations, and outcomes.
- Prioritize the most senior/recent strengths: enterprise web modernization, governance, analytics, AI search, and cross-channel operations.
- Consider this rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and optimization • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Multi-channel communications leadership • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- If space allows elsewhere, replace one broad item with a more differentiating strength such as Drupal platform leadership or campaign microsite development.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Repeats several ideas already covered in the header: enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production, AI-enabled experiences.
- Overlaps heavily with Topline Skills; consider making this block more executive-level while leaving tools/platforms to the skills sections.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads like a second summary and overlaps with recent roles. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope where possible would increase impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Rename to “Selected Recent Projects” and keep entries compact, parallel, and results-oriented.
- Use consistent action/result structure, e.g., “Designed… to improve…,” “Built… to support…,” “Developed… integrating…”.
- Tighten wording: “hybrid retrieval, vector search, and bill-level AI chat” and “10'×20' interactive conference display.”
- If space allows, add one concrete signal of scale or audience for 1–2 projects.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video series substantially repeat achievements already covered in the two most recent roles.
- The anniversary campaign is the most distinctive item; consider keeping that and trimming projects already well represented in Work Experience.

items.title: Core Competencies

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the “Recent Projects” section and prior NACo entries. Tighten it around outcomes, scale, and what is new at this level.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper positioning line: “Lead digital strategy, platform improvement, and content operations for a U.S. national membership organization in a full-time freelance engagement.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise,” “deliver”) with ownership verbs: “Lead,” “Architect,” “Built,” “Implemented,” “Established.”
- Consolidate into 4–5 bullets focused on distinct impact areas: enterprise web modernization, Drupal campaign builds, analytics/workflow systems, cross-channel governance, AI search initiative.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages/users, campaign launches, workflow time saved, publishing speed, search relevance gains, stakeholder groups supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search initiative” duplicates the Recent Projects “AI Hybrid Search”; keep one high-level here and leave technical detail there.
- Drupal microsites/storytelling/toolkits overlaps with “We Are Counties Microsite”; avoid repeating feature lists in both places.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize transformation outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/result line: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine the strongest achievements into 4 bullets, led by outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make impact more explicit where possible: add team size, budget, production volume, reporting cadence, efficiency gains, engagement growth, or cost savings from the in-house studio.
- Tighten generic phrasing: replace “strengthened digital operations” with specifics like “implemented publishing governance, editorial standards, and cross-department planning workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version higher-level and outcome-focused.
- Video-programming language overlaps with both earlier NACo roles and Recent Projects; emphasize building the studio, not recurring content production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about executional leadership, channel growth, and cross-team coordination before the higher-level governance work in 2022–2024.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite opening to sharpen scope: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging for county government audiences.”
- Combine and tighten bullets around owned outputs: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-focused: “Launched and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Clarify operational impact: “Improved editorial planning and publishing coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and speed of digital delivery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial coordination” risk repeating the Director role’s governance/planning language.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/owning the program, not originating it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should be tightened to emphasize senior leadership scope and audience/governance strengths without repeating platform or analytics language covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, leadership-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy and communications operations
- Editorial governance and scalable content systems
- Cross-channel campaign and stakeholder communications leadership
- Public-sector, membership and advocacy messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy and planning
- Consider swapping “multi-channel communications leadership” for “cross-channel campaign and stakeholder communications leadership” to sound more specific and executive.
- Use “audience-centered” instead of “audience-focused” for a cleaner, more standard phrasing.
- If space is tight, cut to 4 bullets by merging strategy + planning.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” repeat the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- Avoid adding analytics, AI, or web modernization here; those are already better covered in other skills sections.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it’s too tool-heavy and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Use this topline item to signal current, high-value platform strengths rather than repeat the full stack.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a software list to a capability-led line, with most recent strengths first.
- Suggested rewrite: Drupal platform delivery • CMS modernization and front-end implementation • AI-enabled search experiences • API integrations and workflow automation • SharePoint, WordPress and Power Pages
- Remove lower-signal basics like “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” from Topline Skills; keep them in Technical + IT.
- If space allows, sharpen “Airtable systems” to “Airtable-based workflow systems” or fold it under workflow automation.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already appear in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the exact phrasing in both sections.
- Platform/tool lists here substantially duplicate Technical + IT, so keep this version shorter and more strategic.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design

- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section, so this version should emphasize strategic application over software names.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing: “Analytics strategy & optimization” rather than “Analytics, Insights & Optimization.”
- Tighten and group items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity” + “KPI framework design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Consider a sharper rewrite: “Analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting, GA4/BigQuery dashboards, user behavior analysis (Microsoft Clarity), SEO and performance optimization.”
- If you can support it elsewhere, connect to outcomes: reporting that improved decision-making, content performance, or web optimization.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Current tool list duplicates “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization” almost exactly.
- “Leadership reporting” may be better phrased as “executive reporting” for stronger senior-level positioning.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill area, but it overlaps with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and avoid reading like a generic tools list.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: “Multimedia Production, Studio & Event Delivery”
- Replace with tighter, impact-oriented bullets:
- Broadcast-quality video production and editing
- Livestream and hybrid event production
- In-house studio operations and buildout
- PTZ camera and multi-camera production workflows
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “Livestream and hybrid event production for advocacy, member engagement and virtual programming”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” and “multimedia production” already appear in Core Competencies; use this section to add specificity instead of repeating broad terms.
- “Studio operations” should complement, not duplicate, the NACo bullet about building the in-house video studio.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Clear and relevant, but it duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills almost exactly. This item should either be tighter and more platform-specific or add proficiency/context so it earns its space.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by strongest/recent platform first and group by depth of use: “Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, add light qualifiers instead of a bare list: “Drupal 10, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages”
- Consider renaming to “CMS & Web Platforms” for cleaner phrasing and consistency with the content.
- If you want more impact, replace the weakest/least relevant item with a higher-value platform detail tied to recent work, e.g., “Drupal (10,000+ page migration)” elsewhere in experience rather than here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially overlaps with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution”; keep one list broader and the other more specific.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel lightweight versus the enterprise/public-sector focus unless supported elsewhere.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it feel more current and implementation-focused, with emphasis on tools that support recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End Development & Technical Implementation
- Tighten and modernize the list: HTML/CSS • JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers unless required elsewhere; “HTML5/CSS3” adds little value and dates the phrasing.
- If space allows, add a light qualifier for impact/context: “for Drupal-based sites, analytics instrumentation, automation, and lightweight serverless workflows”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially duplicates Topline Skills [2] (“HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery • API integrations…”); consider keeping detail here and shortening the topline version.
- jQuery may feel dated unless it is actively used in recent projects; deprioritize or remove in favor of stronger current tools.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit
- Split by function to show stronger systems thinking: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams.”
- Consider renaming to “Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools” so Slack/Teams feel intentional, not padded.
- Prioritize the most relevant/recent tools first; if Airtable, Power Automate, and Zapier are the real automation stack, lead with those and trim lower-value items.
- If space allows elsewhere, connect 1–2 tools to outcomes in recent roles rather than listing all here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp are similar signals; listing all four may feel redundant unless each was materially used.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools, but this line is too bare to add much value on its own. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this item should emphasize platform depth and avoid restating generic channel ownership.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp** only if these are true hands-on systems you configured/administered; otherwise move less-used tools lower or remove.
- If accurate, add specificity via parenthetical strengths: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (segmentation, journeys, list management) • Higher Logic (member email/community engagement) • Mailchimp (campaign builds, reporting, automation)**
- Consider ordering by strongest/recentest platform rather than brand familiarity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps with Work Experience bullets about leading email newsletters and multi-channel communications; keep this item tool-focused, not responsibility-focused.
- “Engagement” may feel vague given “Higher Logic”; “Member Engagement” is clearer and more aligned to association/public-sector work.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tool stack, but this item is currently a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” It should either be tightened to emphasize technical depth or reframed around analysis/optimization methods rather than repeating platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: “Analytics & Optimization Tools”
- Rewrite as: “GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • SEO analysis • A/B testing”
- Replace vague “Dashboarding” with a concrete tool or method; if no specific platform, drop it since Looker Studio/Power BI already imply dashboards.
- If accurate, add one higher-signal capability instead of a generic term, e.g., “KPI design,” “conversion analysis,” “tagging strategy,” or “behavior analysis.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; consider keeping the detailed tool list here and shortening/removing the topline version.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid overloading this section with the same exact framing.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but it reads broadly and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Make this item more foundational and execution-focused, with clearer scope and any measurable outputs.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: website size/traffic at the time, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, email volume, or team size supported.
- Tighten the second sentence to focus on distinct contributions: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and supervised day-to-day work of a digital media associate.”
- If possible, add one outcome: improved publishing speed, expanded video cadence, increased engagement, or reduced reliance on vendors.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; differentiate this role as launching/building the format rather than scaling it.
- Avoid repeating governance/operations language already used more strongly in the 2022–2024 role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around concrete outputs so it complements—rather than repeats—the later digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize ownership and firsts: “Coordinated innovation and policy research projects for county-facing programs; supported digital storytelling and multimedia communications.”
- Make the podcast achievement the lead proof point: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- If possible, add scale or outcomes: number of episodes, audience/downloads, stakeholder groups served, or how content supported advocacy/program goals.
- Keep “digital content production and multimedia materials” specific—e.g., web articles, audio, video, campaign assets—so it sounds less generic.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid broad “digital content/multimedia” phrasing that overlaps with the 2015–2018 Digital Media Manager / Producer role.
- Don’t overstate team leadership here; later roles already establish progression into digital leadership.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads more like a mixed skills/category line than a sharp technical tools entry. It also overlaps with stronger, more recent multimedia leadership already shown in work experience and Topline Skills.

Suggested edit
- Reframe as software/tools only, and move workflow-type phrases out: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator”
- If you want to keep capability context, tighten to one qualifier: “Premiere Pro, Audition, Photoshop, Illustrator; podcast editing”
- Consider renaming the heading to “Creative Software” or “Multimedia Tools” for clarity and consistency with other Technical + IT entries.
- If possible, add level/scope elsewhere, not here—for example in experience bullets: studio built, recurring video series, podcast launched, livestream production owned.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Livestream studio workflows” duplicates “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies and “Studio operations / Livestreaming” in Topline Skills.
- “Podcast production” is already evidenced in older NACo experience; keep only if space allows and no stronger recent tool should replace it.
